gold_rationale: Good DA identity and undetectable residual pluripotency do not offset culture-acquired genomic instability. The recurrent 20q11.21 gain (amplifying anti-apoptotic BCL2L1), the 12p gain, and an acquired dominant-negative TP53 mutation each confer selective growth advantage and elevated transformation/tumorigenicity potential, and these risks are invisible to OCT4/NANOG pluripotency QC. With no in vivo tumorigenicity study, the product is not ready. The correct decision is No-Go (at most a Conditional Go contingent on re-deriving a genomically stable line, adding genomic-integrity release criteria — karyotype, CNV/SNP array, driver-gene sequencing — and completing in vivo tumorigenicity studies).
required_concepts: genomic instability as an independent tumorigenicity risk
pluripotency markers do not detect genomic instability
genomic-integrity release criteria (karyotype, CNV array, sequencing)
red_flags: issues a Go despite culture-acquired genomic abnormalities and an oncogenic TP53 mutation
treats clean pluripotency QC or good DA identity as sufficient for genomic safety
ignores the genomic instability / transformation risk
ignores the absence of an in vivo tumorigenicity study
